subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is an example of qualitative data?
options: A player's sprint time in seconds
A coach's description of a player's attitude
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and subjective, such as a coach's observations of attitude or technique.

questions.q: A skill made up of many subroutines that requires concentration and decision-making is classified as a:
questions.explain: Complex skills involve many subroutines and require attention, judgement and decision-making.

questions.q: The inverted-U theory states that performance is best when arousal is:
questions.explain: The inverted-U theory says performance peaks at an optimal moderate level of arousal and declines if arousal is too low or too high.

questions.q: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body is known as:
questions.explain: Abduction is movement of a body part away from the midline, such as raising the arm sideways.

questions.q: A dribble in football performed while reacting to opponents is classified as a(n):
questions.explain: Open skills are affected by an unpredictable environment, so the performer must constantly adapt.

questions.q: Mixing with others and making friends through sport is an example of which type of well-being?
questions.explain: Social well-being involves interacting with others, cooperating and forming friendships.

questions.q: Anxiety in sport can be described as:
options: A negative emotional state linked to worry or nervousness
questions.explain: Anxiety is a negative emotional state involving feelings of worry, nervousness and apprehension.

questions.q: According to the inverted-U theory, if arousal becomes too high, performance will:
questions.explain: Once arousal passes the optimal point, performance declines because the athlete becomes over-aroused.

questions.q: What does the 'M' in SMART goal setting stand for?
questions.explain: In SMART targets the M stands for Measurable, so progress can be tracked.

questions.q: A marathon runner may 'carbo-load' before a race in order to:
questions.explain: Carbo-loading increases glycogen stores in the muscles, providing more energy for endurance events.

questions.q: Which type of personality is typically calm, reserved and suited to precise, low-arousal activities such as archery?
questions.explain: Introverts are quieter and more reserved, often suited to closed, precise, low-arousal skills.

questions.q: A drawback of relying only on extrinsic motivation, such as rewards, is that:
options: It builds long-lasting love of the sport
The performer may lose interest once the reward is removed
Performers always enjoy the sport more
questions.explain: If a performer is driven only by rewards, their motivation can fall away once those rewards stop.

questions.q: Blood doping is a banned method that works by:
options: Increasing red blood cells to carry more oxygen
Reducing the number of red blood cells
questions.explain: Blood doping raises the red blood cell count so more oxygen can be delivered to the muscles, boosting endurance.

questions.q: Deviance in sport refers to:
options: Behaviour that goes against the accepted norms and rules
questions.explain: Deviance is behaviour such as cheating, doping or violence that breaks the moral or written rules of sport.

questions.q: Which nutrient helps the digestive system work properly and prevents constipation?
questions.explain: Dietary fibre adds bulk to food and aids the movement of food through the digestive system.

questions.q: The multi-stage fitness test (bleep test) measures which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The bleep test estimates aerobic capacity, a measure of cardiovascular endurance.

questions.q: Energy balance is achieved when:
options: Energy intake is greater than energy expenditure
Energy intake is less than energy expenditure
questions.explain: Energy balance occurs when the energy taken in from food equals the energy used by the body.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of quantitative over qualitative data?
options: It is easy to compare and analyse objectively
It is based on personal opinion
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and objective, making it easier to compare and analyse reliably.

questions.q: Which is the best way to help prevent injury during training?
options: Skipping the warm-up to save time
Using correct technique and appropriate equipment
questions.explain: Correct technique, suitable equipment and a proper warm-up all help to reduce the risk of injury.

questions.q: A disadvantage of the media's demand to schedule matches at certain times is that it can:
options: Be inconvenient for live spectators and disrupt players' routines
questions.explain: Media scheduling can move events to awkward times, inconveniencing fans and players to suit broadcasters.

questions.q: What does the 'A' in SMART goal setting stand for?
questions.explain: In SMART targets the A stands for Achievable, so the goal is within the performer's reach.

questions.q: Mental rehearsal is a technique used to:
options: Picture a successful performance to improve focus and reduce anxiety
questions.explain: Mental rehearsal involves visualising a successful performance to improve concentration and control nerves.
